title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). Write G^ for the profinite group \hat{\mathfrak G}^+_{0,3} with generators rho, sigma and relations rho^3 = sigma^2 = 1. It is the profinite completion of Z/3 * Z/2 = PSL_2(Z), the oriented cartographic group.

The group M~_{0,3}, and its subgroup M'~_{0,3}, is an extension of a Galois-type group Gamma~ (a profinite group of Grothendieck-Teichmüller type) by G^, as in (63). It acts on G^. The subgroup M'~_{0,3}[0] consists of 'normalized' automorphisms u. Such a u is given by a pair (xi, eta) in a set Sigma_{rho,sigma} with u(rho) = xi*rho and u(sigma) = eta*sigma. The pair is constrained by the flattened 'loop equations'.

On the previous page Grothendieck fixes a continuous surjection psi: G^ -> G onto a profinite group, in practice a finite one. Combinatorially this is a regular dessin or map, given by rho_G, sigma_G with rho_G^3 = sigma_G^2 = 1.

Definition (69). psi is called effective if, for every u in M'[0], the image pair (xi_G, eta_G) = (psi(xi), psi(eta)) lies in Sigma^{eff}_{rho_G,sigma_G}. That is, there is an automorphism u_G of G with u_G(rho_G) = xi_G rho_G and u_G(sigma_G) = eta_G sigma_G. Equivalently the square (70) commutes: psi∘u = u_G∘psi. Equivalently each such u maps Ker psi into itself.

The margin lists the equivalent conditions:
- a) M'[0] maps into the effective pairs;
- b) every u in M' descends to some u_M on G;
- b') the same for u in M'[0] only;
- c), c') psi extends to a homomorphism psi_M from M' (onto an extension M_{rho_G,sigma_G} of the Galois-type quotient by G).

The equivalence of b and b' uses M' = M'[0]·G^, where G^ acts by inner automorphisms, which preserve the normal subgroup Ker psi. So the condition is automatic when (G, rho_G, sigma_G) satisfy conditions b) of (70), for instance when Ker psi is characteristic or otherwise canonically defined.

Purpose. The next page (Théorème, (71)-(72)) uses effectiveness to build a unique homomorphism phi_M: M' -> M_phi. It is given explicitly on elements u_{alpha,beta,f} by the invariants phi(alpha), phi(beta), phi(f). This yields a morphism of exact sequences 1->G^->M'->Gamma'->1 to 1->G->M_phi->Gamma_phi->1.

In modern terms: a normal finite-index subgroup of \hat{PSL_2(Z)} that is stable under the GT-type group descends that group's action to a finite group G. This gives a 'finite-level' quotient of the GT-type group acting on G. It is the GT-analogue of a dessin whose field of moduli is Q, and of the outer Galois representation Gamma_Q -> Out(G) together with the extension it induces.
errors: Equation labels: the image reads (69) and (70) (consistent with (71)-(72) on the next page), not (19) and (20).
The diagram should read \hat{\mathfrak G}^+_{0,3} rather than \hat{\Gamma}^+_{0,3}.
(xi_G, eta_G) should be (psi(xi), psi(eta)); the transcribed 'u(xi), u(eta)' is a misreading or slip.
No mathematical error. Uniqueness of u_G follows from the surjectivity of psi. The reduction from M' to M'[0] is valid because inner automorphisms preserve the normal subgroup Ker psi.

ideas.what: A finite quotient psi of \hat{PSL_2(Z)} is 'effective' if its kernel is stable under the GT-type automorphism group M'. Equivalently, each normalized automorphism u(rho)=xi rho, u(sigma)=eta sigma descends to an automorphism of G.
ideas.modern_name: GT-stable (Galois-invariant) normal subgroups / regular dessins with field of moduli Q; G-dessins invariant under GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: Galois action on dessins: Grothendieck (Esquisse), Belyi, Schneps, Lochak. GT action on finite G-dessins via pairs of generators: P. Guillot (c. 2014-2016).
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Galois action on dessins only informally; this formal definition is unpublished (Longue Marche continuation notes).

ideas.what: Four equivalent formulations of effectiveness: action on generator pairs, descent of all u, descent of normalized u, extension of psi to M'.
ideas.modern_name: Descent of an automorphism group to a characteristic or invariant quotient

ideas.what: Setup for the theorem on the next page: an effective psi induces a morphism of extensions from the GT-type extension of Gamma' by \hat{PSL_2(Z)} to a finite-level extension 1->G->M_phi->Gamma_phi->1, given explicitly by the loop-equation invariants (alpha, beta, f).
ideas.modern_name: Finite-level GT action / 'GT(G)'-type groups attached to a finite group with two generators of orders 3 and 2
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. Guillot, 'The Grothendieck-Teichmüller group of a finite group and G-dessins d'enfants'

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines, for a finite group G with generators of orders 3 and 2, a condition under which the GT-type group's action descends to G. He then (next page) builds a finite-level image of the GT-type group as an extension of a quotient by G. This anticipates later finite-level GT constructions attached to finite groups, but phrased in the PSL_2(Z) (rho^3 = sigma^2 = 1) setting with his 'loop-equation' invariants.
missed.quote: On dira que psi est effectif si pour u ∈ M'~_{0,3}[0] ... ∃ u_G automorphisme de G tel qu'on ait u_G(rho_G)=xi_G rho_G, u_G(sigma_G)=eta_G sigma_G
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows Grothendieck's own route to 'GT acting on a finite group' through effective quotients of \hat{PSL_2(Z)}. This is relevant to the history of finite-level approximations of GT and to the Galois action on regular dessins, but the definition itself is fairly routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The definition is natural and the equivalences are routine. Its interest is historical: it is Grothendieck's unpublished formalization of GT-stable finite quotients, leading to a finite-level morphism of extensions akin to later work (e.g. Guillot).
transcription_corrections: Equation numbers are (69) and (70), not (19) and (20); likewise 'conditions b) de (70)'.
Margin: 'l'introduire par conditions équivalentes', followed by a), b), b'), c), c'), 'On dira dans ce cas que psi est effectif', referring to (70) b) and (69).
Margin item a) appears to read 'M'~_{0,3}[0] -> Sigma^{eff}_{rho,sigma} ⊂ Aut' (the map lands in the effective pairs).
